extracted.intended_audience: UW School of Nursing applicants preparing NIH research project grant applications (investigators writing proposals under the NIH Simplified Review Framework)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing NIH research project grant applications submitted under the NIH Simplified Review Framework (SRF), emphasizing what reviewers will prioritize and how applicants should present importance, rigor/feasibility, and team/resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Should this research be done? If so, why? Applicants must clearly articulate the scientific importance of their work—not just its relevance to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the research question in a compelling way; demonstrate how the work addresses a significant gap in knowledge; avoid jargon and make the case accessible to a broad scientific audience. A clear, persuasive rationale for the study’s importance can set the tone for the entire review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Can it be done well? If so, how? Reviewers are being encouraged to avoid nitpicking and instead focus on whether the proposed approach is rigorous and feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a well-structured, logical plan; anticipate potential challenges and describe how they’ll be addressed; emphasize methodological soundness without overwhelming the reader with excessive detail. The goal is to instill confidence that the research can be executed effectively even if every contingency isn’t fully mapped out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the right people and tools in place to do it? This factor is evaluated categorically rather than numerically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe the qualifications of the team as they relate to the project; highlight access to necessary facilities, equipment, and institutional support. Avoid over-relying on reputation; focus on relevance and readiness. Note scoring: this factor is evaluated as either “appropriate” or “additional expertise/resources needed,” with comments required only if gaps are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring mechanics under the SRF
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers record scores under the Simplified Review Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of the first two factors (Importance; Rigor and Feasibility) is scored on a 1–9 scale. The third factor (Expertise and Resources) is not numerically scored but marked as “appropriate” or “additional expertise/resources needed,” and reviewers must provide comments only when gaps are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional considerations (scope of review and impact factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics that remain relevant to overall impact or have been deemphasized under the SRF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRF reduces the burden of additional review criteria so reviewers can stay focused on science. Human subjects protections and similar issues can still affect the overall impact score. By contrast, budget and resource authentication no longer directly affect scoring. Overall guidance: 'less is more'—avoid distracting administrative detail so reviewers can concentrate on scientific importance and feasibility.
